newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ economy not hurt by coalition talks - Peters.
newsitem.headline: NZ economy not hurt by coalition talks - Peters.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters said on Thursday there was no evidence protracted coalition negotiations were hurting the economy.
"There is not a shred of evidence showing any unusual change from the pre-election period to the post-election one," he said.

Earlier, the New Zealand Press Association reported that mayors and business leaders in the country's capital wanted a quick end to the coalition talks, saying political procrastination was delaying investment and spending.
Peters said the talks were proceeding with all urgency possible, and New Zealand would pay if there was any undue haste.
"The country is not being hurt by this necessary period of coalition talks," Peters said.
"International evidence from similar talks is that the longer the talks take, the more stable the resulting government," he said.
